hook_text: Stand on any South African street corner and you can count three different governments in one minute.
clip_script: The police van on the corner? National government pays those officers. The clinic queue across the road and the school next to it? Your province runs both. The tap you drank from this morning, the street light and the refuse truck? That is your municipality. One street, three governments. South Africa's Constitution calls them spheres: national, led by the President; nine provinces, each led by a Premier; and two hundred and fifty-seven municipalities, each led by a mayor and councillors. And inside government there are three jobs kept apart on purpose: Parliament makes the laws, the President and ministers carry them out, and the courts judge. Why apart? Because a player who is also the referee never loses. So next time the water is off, you know exactly whose door to knock on.
visual_style: A whiteboard street drawn in one line, with a police van, a clinic, a school, a tap and a refuse truck, each circled and labelled national, provincial or local; then three boxes labelled make, do, judge.
mood: Street-smart and practical, ending in a confident civic punchline.
pacing: Quick pointing tour of the street, a steady count of the three spheres, a sharp final line.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and match every service to its government.
